title: Skipping an encoded argument list
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w,E$ be bit strings, and let $o$ be an oracle on bit strings. Suppose that on every encoding of a natural number $p$, the oracle returns the $p$th bit of $E$, defaulting to false beyond its end, and that $E$ has length at most $B$. For every list $as$ and every register state $p,c,a$ such that $E$ after position $p$ consists of the encoding of $as$ followed by a suffix, with $c,a\le B$, there is an $a'\le B$ such that the machine can move from its argument-list scan state with registers $(p,c,a)$ to the gate scan state with registers $(p+|\operatorname{encode}(as)|,c,a')$, while all configurations before the endpoint keep every register at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle answers on encoded natural numbers equal the corresponding E bit, defaulting to false
E.drop p equals the encoding of as followed by rest
